newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ban Hin Lee Bank starts asset management.
newsitem.headline: Ban Hin Lee Bank starts asset management.

text.p: Malaysia's Ban Hin Lee Bank Bhd on Wednesday announced it was setting up an asset management subsidiary in technical collaboration with Rothschild Asset Management, Singapore.
BHLB Asset Management (BAM) Sdn Bhd would focus on providing portfolio management services to high net worth individuals in the country, its managing director Philip Angers said.
"Our aim is to be recognised as Malaysia's most ethical, prudent and consistently out-performing fund manager by balancing risks and returns," Angers said at the launch of the company.
BAM already manages the funds of BHLB Pacific Trust Management Bhd, a private unit trust company and subsidiary of Ban Hin Lee Bank. It has an existing list of high net worth clients, Angers said.

Malaysia's Deputy Finance Minister Wong See Wah said the unit trust industry was worth 56 billion ringgit in Malaysia, but accounted for just 7.5 percent of the market capitalisation on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange.
He said despite there being 81 licensed fund managers, there was room for the industry to grow.
Malaysia's Securities Commission had specifically identified fund management as an area to be developed in its 1995-97 business plan.

"Among the areas the (Securities Commission) has and is looking at are the formulation of a national policy on fund management, streamlining of the regulatory framework, deregulation of institutional funds, and development of a collective investment schemes industry," Wong said.
These along with some tax incentives announced in the 1997 annual budget should help develop the Malaysian fund industry, the minister said. -- Kuala Lumpur newsroom (603-230 7509)
